program_analysis.summary: This program implements a transductive semi-supervised classifier using a frozen DINOv2 backbone to extract image embeddings. It employs class-conditional Gaussian modeling and EM-style refinement with unlabeled data to enhance classification accuracy. The method incorporates confidence-gated pseudo-labeling and final nearest-centroid cosine calibration for robust predictions. The approach is designed to be data-efficient and stable, leveraging unlabeled data effectively while keeping the backbone model frozen.

This program implements a semi-supervised learning approach using a frozen DINOv2 backbone to extract image embeddings. It trains a transductive Gaussian class model in feature space with an Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm on unlabeled data. The model estimates class geometry using a few labeled examples and unlabeled data, making it data-efficient. The approach incorporates soft responsibilities and class-prior regularization to refine class means and covariance iteratively.

The program implements a semi-supervised learning framework using a Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone with DINOv2 for feature extraction. It employs a prototype refinement strategy to improve classification accuracy on labeled and unlabeled data. The model is calibrated using a cosine calibrator to enhance prediction reliability. Data augmentation techniques are applied to improve model robustness during training.

The program implements a semi-supervised learning framework using a Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone for image classification. The model extracts features from images and predicts categories based on learned prototypes. Data augmentation techniques are applied to improve generalization.
